steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Shift: Move from describing ("This shows Macbeth is ambitious") to analysing ("Shakespeare presents ambition as destructive through the metaphor of..."). | Always ask: HOW does the writer create this effect? Never just state WHAT happens - explain HOW it's achieved through language, form, and structure. | Top Tip: A Grade 9 critical style is invisible — the examiner does not notice your language because it sounds authoritative and effortless. The quickest way to lose marks is to write informally or to describe the plot. Before the exam, memorise 5-7 analytical verbs (presents, implies, conveys, subverts, reinforces, emphasises, challenges) and commit to never using "shows" or "uses" again.
